title: The Will of Windrow House
premise: Silas Eastwick, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, is hired by a wealthy widow who pays in advance to prove her husband's death was natural — before the statute expires and the policy pays out to someone who may have killed him. Digging into Windrow House, Silas finds a household of servants and wards bound by fierce loyalty to the dead man, each hiding pieces of a ledger hidden in plain sight in the house's wallpaper patterns. As the deadline closes, Silas realizes the client herself orchestrated the investigation to expose the true killer: the family lawyer, whose forged identity conceals a decades-old theft. In the end, Silas must choose between protecting the found family that sheltered her from her own erased past and delivering the truth that will destroy their home.
about_author: Dominic Delacroix is the pen name of a former claims adjuster turned novelist who spent fifteen years reading the fine print of other people's tragedies. He writes mysteries about paper trails, quiet houses, and the people who memorize both.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Silas Eastwick's POV. A retainer arrives from Vivienne Ashcombe, widow of Gerald Ashcombe, demanding proof — not suspicion — that his death was natural before the policy's statute expires in thirty days. At Windrow House, Silas photographs every room, and her photographic memory snags on something impossible: the same floral motif repeating in the wallpaper with deliberate irregularities. The beat is wary curiosity; Silas, who trusts patterns over people, senses she's been hired for reasons no one will name.

chapters.title: The Household That Remembers
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with interludes from housekeeper Maren Cole. Interviews reveal a staff that functions less as employees than as family: Maren, gardener Tobias, and ward Ilsa all deflect questions with practiced warmth while guarding Gerald's study. Silas decodes the wallpaper irregularities as a numeric cipher matching entries in Gerald's old account ledgers — records of payments to someone named 'R. Vane.' The beat deepens into belonging; Silas, orphaned with no records of her own childhood, feels dangerously at home.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The cipher resolves: R. Vane is the family lawyer, Rowan Vance, who has been siphoning the estate for twenty years under a stolen identity — and Gerald discovered it days before his 'natural' death. When Silas confronts Vance, he reveals he knows what she is: a child of Windrow House itself, placed out and scrubbed from its records long ago. The beat is betrayal and vertigo; the case has become personal, and the statute clock runs down to seventy-two hours.

chapters.title: What the Walls Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Silas and Vivienne. Climax at Windrow House on the final night — Vance returns to burn the decoded ledger, and the household, loyal to truth over comfort, helps Silas trap him with the original wallpaper panels as evidence. Resolution: Vance confesses; Gerald's death stands natural after all, but the estate passes to the household, not the lawyer. Vivienne admits she hired Silas hoping she'd recognize the house. Silas chooses truth and stays — found family, finally claimed.
